sphere_commentary.overview:
The single-volume dataset (VOL001) shows broadly consistent positive responses across all 30 protocols, with HEALING leading on volume and consistency, THRIVING producing the highest peaks, and TRANSFORMING showing the widest variance — patterns consistent with each series' design intent.
• HEALING (n=574) anchors the aggregate with a 6.98 mean and the tightest overall std, anchored by H-OS-L1 (n=95) and H-SL-L1 (n=54).
• THRIVING (n=245) matches HEALING's mean (6.96) but with T-FC-L3 (Summit) the standout high performer at 7.63.
• TRANSFORMING (n=181) trails at 6.59 mean with the widest variance, carrying X-MC-L3 as the dataset's lowest-scoring protocol.
• YouTube reach is universally minimal (max 30 views) — a reach ceiling rather than an efficacy ceiling for most protocols.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The three series exhibit efficacy profiles that align with their therapeutic intents, with the clearest divergence between observed means and AutoGluon predictions occurring in TRANSFORMING.
• HEALING protocols cluster tightly around 7.0 across all entry points, with low distress (Anxiety, Over-stimulation, Sleep) producing the strongest and most consistent outcomes.
• THRIVING holds steady 6.7–7.6, with Focus & Clarity ascending through levels (T-FC-L1=6.46 → T-FC-L3=7.63) suggesting a genuine level effect, not noise.
• TRANSFORMING displays the broadest range (5.7–7.2); AutoGluon predicts substantially higher efficacy for several X-series protocols than observed, suggesting underperformance or population mismatch.
• Cross-bucket routing from AutoGluon repeatedly surfaces X-ME-L1 as relevant to overstimulation, crisis, focus, and maintenance — the most analytically mobile protocol in the dataset.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols diverge meaningfully from expected patterns, either in score, variance, or model alignment.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10) records the lowest mean in the library (5.70) with the highest std (2.45) — a bimodal distribution pattern suggesting population mismatch or design failure at L3.
• H-CR-L2 (n=33) shows a 1.4-point gap between observed mean (6.52) and AutoGluon crisis-zone prediction (7.96) — the model's strongest underprediction.
• X-MD-L3 (n=13) shows the most extreme cross-run drift (sim=0.507) coupled with high variance (std=2.38) — analytical instability warrants explicit caution.
• T-MB series shows uniformly high drift across all three levels (0.554–0.578) — the most systematically unstable analytical framing in the dataset.
• T-FC-L3 (n=35) holds the highest THRIVING mean (7.63) yet has only 15 YouTube views — a strong efficacy signal that remains undiscovered by audience.
• X-ME-L1 is the most cross-bucketed protocol (routed to 5 zones by AutoGluon) but observed mean (6.74) sits below all predicted scores.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Patterns across multiple signal layers support targeted protocol and routing interventions.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10) — low mean, bimodal distribution, 'too busy' rhythm feedback from 4/17 → redesign the L3 descent arc or retire this variant; investigate whether the L3 depth exceeds effective entrainment range.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L3 (n=35, mean=7.63) — highest THRIVING score, strong qualitative praise, 11/29 reporting significant improvement → promote as flagship Focus protocol and address the visibility gap (only 15 YouTube views).
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-ME-L1 (n=39) — cross-bucketed to 5 zones by AutoGluon with predicted scores 7.5–8.2 but observed mean only 6.74 → investigate why real-world performance lags model prediction; possible routing or population mismatch.
• H-CR-L2 (n=33) — AutoGluon's top crisis prediction (7.96) vs observed 6.52 → test as primary crisis anchor and adjust routing in the Adviser to surface it for acute distress entries.
• X-MD-L1 (n=22) — pct_pos only 45% against AutoGluon prediction of 7.88 → increase hold phase or adjust the ASCENT arc; the model expects more from this design than it delivers.
• T-MB series (n=14–25) — uniform high drift across L1/L2/L3 → groove redesign candidate; the analytical instability suggests listener perception is genuinely shifting or the sound design is not landing.
• H-CR-L3 (n=27) — settle mode bimodal (7 immediate, 5 at 5-min) with 4/19 music 'not liked' → consider a lighter groove variant for acute-distress listeners who need fast settling without music friction.
• H-OS-L1 (n=95, mean=7.15) — strongest single protocol in HEALING yet only 30 YouTube views → priority candidate for playlist surfacing and Adviser routing optimisation.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is widespread across the protocol library, while semantic clustering remains unavailable due to sparse embedding history.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 24 of 30 protocols show notable drift (similarity < 0.85), with strongest signals in X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), X-ME-L2 (0.532), and T-MB-L3 (0.554); this likely reflects genuine analytical evolution as data accumulates rather than instability in the model itself.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Too few protocols with embeddings for cluster analysis — cannot yet identify whether protocols cluster by zone, by outcome profile, or by listener type.
• Confidence note: Drift metrics are reliable at the protocol level, but interpretive depth is limited by sparse embedding history; treat drift direction as hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive.

AutoGluon predicts 7.96 for H-CR-L2 specifically (not L1), suggesting L2 is the model's preferred crisis anchor. YouTube views at 6 are minimal.
by_protocol.H-CR-L2: n=33, mean=6.52, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution peaks at 7 with a long left tail. Qualitative data (n=16) shows 6 moderate, 5 noticeable, 4 significant improvement ratings; settle times split between 5 and 10 minutes; music opinion notably polarised (6 neutral, 5 loved). AutoGluon ranks this as the top crisis protocol with a predicted 7.96 — the largest model-vs-observation gap in the crisis zone (~1.4 points). YouTube views at 4 are minimal. Panel converged that this is a strong candidate for promoted routing despite modest observed mean.
by_protocol.H-CR-L3: n=27, mean=6.52, std=1.91, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows the widest spread among crisis protocols, with 4 respondents at scores 1–3 and 3 at score 10. Qualitative data (n=19) indicates 7/19 settled within the first minute — the fastest crisis protocol — but also 4/19 disliked the music, the highest negative music rating in the crisis set. YouTube views at 5 are minimal. The panel read this as a protocol with fast efficacy potential but a music-friction problem that may cost it ratings.
by_protocol.H-OS-L1: n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78, confidence=strong (VOL001 only). This is the highest-n protocol in the library; distribution leans positive with score 8 as the mode (26 respondents) and a moderate left tail. Qualitative data (n=29) shows 12/29 reporting noticeable improvement, settle times at ~10 minutes (11), with strong music reception (19/29 liked or loved). YouTube reach is the dataset's highest at 30 views, though still modest. AutoGluon predicts 6.86 for overstimulation, ~0.3 below observed — the model under-predicts this protocol, suggesting its groove or arc carries signal not captured by design features alone.
by_protocol.H-OS-L2: n=51, mean=6.92, std=1.73, confidence=strong (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 14 respondents at score 7 with a right tail at 9–10. Qualitative data (n=21) shows 10/21 reporting noticeable improvement, settle times at ~10 minutes (10); music opinion splits 10 liked vs 6 neutral. YouTube views at 5 are negligible. AutoGluon predicts 6.86 — close to observed — and cross-bucket routes X-ME-L1 and X-ME-L2 here, suggesting shared regulatory mechanisms.
by_protocol.H-OS-L3: n=47, mean=7.04, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 11 respondents at score 7 with 6 at 8. Qualitative data (n=23) shows 10/23 reporting noticeable improvement; 8/23 used the protocol while trying to sleep, the highest sleep-intent use of any over-stimulation protocol. Music opinion (11 liked, 5 neutral) and rhythm opinion balanced. YouTube views at 8 are modest. Notable cross-run drift (sim=0.679) suggests the analytical reading of this protocol is still evolving.
by_protocol.H-SL-L1: n=54, mean=7.19, std=1.86, confidence=strong (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 11 respondents at score 9 with a moderate spread. Qualitative data (n=15) shows 6/15 reporting noticeable, 5/15 moderate, 3/15 significant improvement; settle times split between 5 min (5) and immediate (3). Music reception is strong (13/15 liked or loved). YouTube views at 4 are minimal. The panel noted this protocol has high cross-run drift (sim=0.530) — the second-highest drift in the dataset — warranting explicit confidence hedging on any single-run readings.
by_protocol.H-SL-L2: n=45, mean=7.09, std=1.55, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution is tighter than H-SL-L1 (std 1.55 vs 1.86) with concentration at scores 6–8. Qualitative data (n=15) shows a notable listener-type shift — only 4 self-listeners, 6 caregivers observing patients, 5 supporting dependents — reflecting this protocol's positioning for dependent populations. Settle times extend to 10–20 min (7 and 3 respondents respectively); rhythm opinion shows 3/15 found it too busy. YouTube views at 5 are minimal.
by_protocol.H-SL-L3: n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 7 respondents at score 7 and 3 at score 9. Qualitative data (n=22) shows 7/22 reporting noticeable, 5/22 moderate, 5/22 significant improvement; settle times at ~5 min (8) or ~10 min (5); rhythm balanced or slightly busy. YouTube views at 3 are the lowest in HEALING. Notable cross-run drift (sim=0.611) suggests evolving analytical framing.
by_protocol.T-CF-L1: n=34, mean=6.74, std=1.73, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 8 respondents at score 7 with a left tail at 1–3 (3 respondents). Qualitative data (n=21) shows 8/21 reporting only slight improvement — the highest 'slight' rating in the T-CF series — but balanced by 5/21 reporting significant improvement, suggesting a bimodal experience. Settle times are notably fast (6 immediate, 6 at 10 min). YouTube views at 2 are negligible. Cross-run drift (sim=0.730) is moderate.
by_protocol.T-CF-L2: n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution is tight (std 1.41, the lowest in T-CF) with concentration at scores 6–7. Qualitative data (n=15) shows 5/15 reporting significant improvement — proportionally the highest in T-CF — with settle times at ~10 min (5) or ~5 min (4); music reception is strong (12/15 liked or loved). YouTube views at 2 are negligible. Cross-run drift (sim=0.682) is moderate.
by_protocol.T-CF-L3: n=18, mean=7.28, std=1.32, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 5 respondents at score 9 and 5 at score 7 — the highest mean in the T-CF series despite low n. Qualitative data (n=25, the largest qualitative context in T-CF) shows 7/25 noticeable, 6/25 significant improvement; settle times at ~10 min (7) or ~5 min (7); music opinion is notably split (9 liked, 7 neutral). YouTube views at 7 are modest. Cross-run drift (sim=0.602) is notable.
by_protocol.T-FC-L1: n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 12 respondents at score 7 with a left tail at 1–3 (4 respondents). Qualitative data (n=23) shows 10/23 reporting noticeable, 6/23 significant improvement; settle times split between 5 min (7) and immediate (6) — the fastest Focus settle. Rhythm opinion is notably busy: 9/23 found it slightly busy. YouTube views at 5 are minimal. Cross-run drift (sim=0.614) is moderate.
by_protocol.T-FC-L2: n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 10 respondents at score 8 and 6 at 7. Caregiving and therapy are the dominant use contexts (5 and 4 respectively). YouTube views at 4 are minimal. Cross-run drift (sim=0.633) is moderate.
by_protocol.T-FC-L3: n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution is bimodal with 10 respondents at score 10 and a cluster at 5–7. This is the highest mean in THRIVING and the second-highest in the entire library. Qualitative data (n=29, the largest qualitative context in THRIVING) shows 11/29 reporting significant improvement — the highest count in the library — with settle times at ~10 min (15) and music reception strong (20/29 liked or loved). YouTube views at 15 are the highest in THRIVING but still modest. AutoGluon predicts 7.73, ~0.1 below observed — strong convergence. Cross-run drift (sim=0.532) is notable.
by_protocol.T-MB-L1: n=25, mean=7.04, std=1.34, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution is tight (std 1.34, the lowest in THRIVING) with concentration at 7–8. Qualitative data (n=23) shows 6/23 reporting moderate improvement; settle times are slow — 9/23 settled at ~20 minutes, the slowest in the dataset. Music opinion is split (6 liked, 6 neutral). YouTube views at 3 are minimal. Cross-run drift (sim=0.578) is notable. The panel read this as a protocol that works but demands patience.
by_protocol.T-MB-L2: n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 7 respondents at score 8 but a wide spread (std 2.03). Qualitative data (n=16) shows 5/16 noticeable, 4/16 moderate improvement; settle times at ~5 min (6) or ~10 min (4); rhythm opinion splits between balanced (7) and slightly busy (7). YouTube views at 4 are minimal. Cross-run drift (sim=0.569) is notable. AutoGluon predicts 7.69 for T-MB-L3 — the prediction targets L3, not L2.
by_protocol.T-MB-L3: n=14, mean=6.93, std=1.73, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 7 respondents at score 7. Qualitative data (n=19) shows 6/19 reporting noticeable, 4/19 moderate improvement; critically, 4/19 reported 'Did NOT settle' — the highest non-settling rate in THRIVING. YouTube views at 3 are minimal. Cross-run drift (sim=0.554) is the highest in T-MB series. AutoGluon predicts 7.69 for T-MB-L3, ~0.8 above observed.
by_protocol.X-MC-L1: n=24, mean=6.75, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 7 respondents at score 6 and 5 at 7. by_protocol.X-MC-L2: n=16, mean=6.81, std=1.64, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 5 respondents at score 7 and 4 at 6. by_protocol.X-MC-L3: n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). This is the lowest-scoring protocol in the library. Qualitative data (n=17) shows 9/17 reporting noticeable, 3/17 moderate improvement; rhythm opinion is notably negative — 4/17 found it too busy. YouTube views at 8. Cross-run drift (sim=0.657). by_protocol.X-MD-L1: n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 4 respondents at score 6 and 4 at 7, but a wide left tail (4 at scores 1–3). by_protocol.X-MD-L2: n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 4 respondents at score 6 but with a spread to scores 1–9. Qualitative data (n=21) shows 6/21 noticeable, 5/21 moderate, 5/21 slight improvement — a notably flat outcome distribution; settle times at ~20 min (5) or ~10 min (5). by_protocol.X-MD-L3: n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). by_protocol.X-ME-L1: n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 7 respondents at score 7 and 7 at 8. YouTube views at 8 are modest. AutoGluon routes this protocol to overstimulation, crisis, low, focus, and maintenance zones — the most cross-bucketed protocol in the library — with predicted scores ranging 7.5–8.2, all above the observed 6.74. This is the strongest cross-bucket signal in the dataset.
by_protocol.X-ME-L2: n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 8 respondents at score 7 and 5 at 8. Qualitative data (n=15) shows 7/15 reporting significant improvement — the highest in X-ME — with settle times bimodal (4 at 20 min, 4 immediate). Music reception is strong (13/15 liked or loved). YouTube views at 8 are modest. Cross-run drift (sim=0.532) is notable. AutoGluon routes this to overstimulation, crisis, low, maintenance, and mind-clarity zones.
by_protocol.X-ME-L3: n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing (VOL001 only). Distribution shows 5 respondents at score 7 but with a left tail of 4 at scores 1–3. Qualitative data (n=25) shows 9/25 noticeable improvement but also 5/25 reported no effect — the highest no-effect rate in TRANSFORMING; settle times at ~5 min (8) or ~10 min (6). Music reception is strong (11/25 liked, 7 loved). YouTube views at 4 are minimal. Cross-run drift (sim=0.627) is notable.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Many people find this protocol helps with anxiety, settling within about ten minutes. The music and rhythm land well — it's a reliable choice, even if not many have discovered it yet.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: A steady anxiety protocol that most people find at least somewhat helpful. It works quickly for many, though a few find the music just okay.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Helps with anxiety especially in therapy and caregiving contexts. Some people settle right in, while others take longer — a flexible option.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Used in moments of acute distress, and many people feel genuinely better within minutes. The music is well-liked, though it's rarely reached online.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: The model thinks this could be the strongest crisis option, and many listeners do feel real improvement. It deserves more visibility than it currently gets.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Fast-acting for crisis moments, especially while working or studying. Some people don't connect with the sound — a lighter version might help.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: One of the most-used and best-received protocols in the library. People settle in around ten minutes and genuinely enjoy the music — a clear go-to for overstimulation.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Calms overstimulation reliably, though some find the music just neutral. It's effective but not yet reaching many listeners.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Often chosen when trying to sleep after overstimulation. Most people like it and settle within minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Helps many people wind down, especially during therapy sessions. The music is well-loved and settling happens quickly — a strong sleep companion.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Mostly used by people supporting others, and most find it helpful. A small number find the rhythm too busy — worth knowing if you're sensitive.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Gently eases people toward sleep within minutes. It's well-received but has very few listeners so far.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Some people feel a creative lift right away, while others notice only a small shift. It works fast for those it works for.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: A few people feel a strong creative boost, especially while sleeping or commuting. The music is loved by many who try it.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: The most uplifting option for creative flow in the set, helping some people fall asleep or focus deeply. Music opinions are mixed, but outcomes trend positive.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Helps some people focus quickly, though a fair number find the rhythm a bit busy. Fast to settle, but not for everyone.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Supports focus well, especially in caregiving and therapy contexts. Music opinions vary — it reaches few but works for those who find it.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The standout focus protocol — many people report significant improvement and love the music. It deserves far more visibility than it has.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Balances mood for many, though it takes patience — settling can take up to twenty minutes. Music opinions are split.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Helps some with maintenance and balance, but responses are quite varied. The rhythm feels slightly busy to a notable share of listeners.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Some people find it helpful for ongoing balance, though a few can't settle into it. Worth trying with patience.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Helps many with mental clarity, and the music is well-loved. A small number find it makes things worse — worth a gentle first listen.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Many people feel a significant clarity shift, settling quickly. It's the most viewed in its set, though still few overall.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: The weakest protocol in the library right now — responses are very mixed, and some find the rhythm too busy. Needs redesign or retirement.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Some people feel real motivation lift, but responses vary widely. The data suggests this protocol should work better than it currently does.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Mild help with motivation for many, though outcomes spread across the spectrum. Music is loved by those who connect with it.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Higher average scores but very mixed responses — some people find it transformative, others barely connect. Use with patience.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Many feel meaningful mood and energy lift, and the music is widely loved. The data hints this protocol could help far more people than it currently reaches.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Often produces significant improvement, especially for those who settle. Music is strong, and settling time varies by person.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Mixed results — some feel real improvement, others notice nothing. Music is well-liked; the experience varies by individual.
